Reference · vLLM 0.26.0

How the prompt gets assembled

From the msgs list in run_appworld.py, to the string of token ids the engine actually receives, how many hands does it pass through in between. In the diagram, everything that is our own code is marked in cyan; everything gray is vLLM's.

First separate the three things all called "system"; the whole page uses these three names:

NameWhat it isWho writes it
The system message in the requestmsgs[0], its content is the SYSTEM constantUs
harmony's system messagemodel identity, knowledge cutoff, date, reasoning level, channel instructionsvLLM
harmony's developer message# Instructions plus the full text of our passagevLLM builds the shell, we fill the contents

chat mode: we only hand over messages, the server does the assembly

Cyan = code in our repo Gray = vLLM's code Dashed line = this path exists but wasn't taken this time

What the assembled result looks like

Decoding the output of steps 8–10 above back into text, step 0 in full looks like this (cyan background is text we sent, amber background is what vLLM added itself):

<|start|>system<|message|>You are ChatGPT, a large language model trained by OpenAI.
Knowledge cutoff: 2024-06
Current date: 2026-08-06

Reasoning: high

# Valid channels: analysis, commentary, final. Channel must be
included for every message.<|end|><|start|>developer<|message|># Instructions

You are an autonomous agent operating a phone-like environment on
behalf of your supervisor.

Rules:
- Each turn, write exactly ONE ```python ... ``` code block. …
  (full text of the SYSTEM constant, omitted here)
- When the task is fully done, call apis.supervisor.complete_task()
  (pass answer=... if the task asks a question).<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Task from supervisor: Give me a comma-separated list of top 4 most
played r&b song titles from across my Spotify song, album and
playlist libraries.<|end|><|start|>assistant

Obtained on 2026-08-06 by re-rendering with the harmony encoder in envs/vllm-env, following the same order as online_renderer.py:183-221, 345 tokens. The task text is taken from one entry in AppWorld's test_normal.

Starting from step 1, past assistant turns carry a channel tag, and everything else is appended to the tail unchanged:

…<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>I'll start by exploring the available apps.

```python
print(apis.api_docs.show_app_descriptions())
```<|end|><|start|>user<|message|>Execution output:
[{'name': 'api_docs', 'description': 'An app to search and explore
API documentation.'}]<|end|><|start|>assistant

Step 1 of the same re-render, 402 tokens. The 345 tokens from step 0 are its prefix, exactly, without a single token off.

raw mode: reversed, assembly happens on our side

The boundary between the two chains is exactly reversed. In chat mode, what we hand over is four messages, and the final prompt contains a whole section (model identity, current date, channel instructions) that we never wrote; in raw mode, every character in the final prompt is one we typed. The single --api switch does not change the format, it changes "who decides what the model sees."

Which cell is nondeterministic

The Current date line in step 8 of the diagram above comes from datetime.datetime.now(). vLLM itself left a comment right there at harmony_utils.py:134:

# NOTE(woosuk): This brings non-determinism in vLLM.
# Set VLLM_SYSTEM_START_DATE to pin it.

The launch script launch_vllm_awdiag.py never sets VLLM_SYSTEM_START_DATE. So rerunning the same task on a different day changes one character on line 3 of the prompt, and none of the preceding tokens line up anymore — this is the one single cell in the whole chain that our code has no control over.
